chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah al-Barqi, from his father, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr al-Khazzaz, from Amr ibn Shimir, from Jabir al-Ja'fi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Have a good opinion of God, and know that for Paradise there are eight gates, the width of each of which is a journey of forty years.
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about having a good opinion of God and the structure of Paradise's gates?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) links the spiritual virtue of *hasan al-zann* (good opinion of God) with the tangible reality of Paradise’s eight gates, each spanning a forty-year journey. This description underscores the Shia emphasis on divine mercy and the immense scale of reward for those who maintain hopeful trust in God’s promise.
